nodes.title: Admissibility on primary torsion representations
nodes.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension E/Q_p, with maximal ideal m and residue field k. In the existing O-linear smooth category for a p-adic Lie group H, restrict to objects V in which every vector is killed by a power of m. Call V torsion-admissible when V^U[m^j] has finite O-length for every compact open U and j≥1; call it locally torsion-admissible when each O[H]v is torsion-admissible. Finite generation and finite length retain the existing module predicates over O[H].
proofSteps: Take the full subcategory of primary torsion objects of the supplied smooth category.
Define bounded torsion invariants as the intersection of U-fixed vectors and the kernel of m^j, and apply the existing length predicate.
acceptance: Bounded-exponent objects agree with ordinary admissibility over O/m^j; no global exponent is required.

nodes.title: The augmented Iwasawa algebra
nodes.statement: For p-adic Lie H and compact open U, form A_H=O[H]⊗_{O[U]}O[[U]] as a left O[H]-module. It has a unique associative O-algebra structure extending both O[H] and O[[U]], with the tensor relations identifying the two O[U] actions. For another compact open U′ there is a canonical algebra isomorphism commuting with the H and completed compact subgroup maps. Every smooth primary torsion O[H]-module extends uniquely to A_H.
proofSteps: Use coset representatives H/U to express finite sums with coefficients in O[[U]].
For two compact opens pass to a common open normal subgroup of their intersection; continuity on finite quotients makes multiplication and comparison independent of representatives.
For a vector choose an open subgroup fixing it and a coefficient exponent killing it; the completed coefficients then act through a finite quotient.
acceptance: The tensor expression is a module description; multiplication is the crossed group algebra multiplication, not componentwise tensor multiplication.

nodes.title: Finite presentation in the smooth category
nodes.statement: For smooth primary torsion V, finite presentation means that there are compact opens U_1,U_2 and smooth finite O-length representations W_i of U_i with an exact sequence c-Ind_{U_1}^H W_1 → c-Ind_{U_2}^H W_2 → V → 0. Finite generation is equivalent to being a quotient of one such compact induction, and to finite generation over A_H. Finite presentation is equivalent to finite presentation as an A_H-module; it is not defined as finite presentation over the abstract group ring O[H].
proofSteps: Use smoothness and primary torsion to put finitely many generators in a finite O-length compact-open-stable submodule.
Compact induction generates that module under H.
Use the completed compact group algebra presentation to identify the finite-relation condition with finite presentation over A_H.
acceptance: All three finite-generation formulations agree; the presentation uses compact induction with open support modulo U_i.

nodes.title: Exact-sequence and finite-index calculus
nodes.statement: In a short exact sequence 0→V_1→V_2→V_3→0 of smooth primary torsion H-representations: finite type is extension-stable; if V_1,V_3 are finitely presented then V_2 is finitely presented; if V_2 is finitely presented and V_1 finite type then V_3 is finitely presented; if V_2 is finite type and V_3 finitely presented then V_1 is finite type. nodes.title: Coherence for amalgams of compact open groups
nodes.statement: If a p-adic Lie group H is an amalgam U_1*_{U_0}U_2 of two compact open subgroups over their open intersection, A_H is left coherent. Consequently the finitely presented smooth primary torsion H-representations form an abelian subcategory. This applies to SL_2(F); for GL_2(F) use H_0={g:det g∈O_F^×}, its amalgam decomposition, and the index-two subgroup H_0 of G′=GL_2(F)/⟨varpi_F I_2⟩. Thus finitely presented G′-representations form an abelian subcategory.
proofSteps: Identify A_H with the amalgam of O[[U_1]] and O[[U_2]] over O[[U_0]].
The compact group rings are noetherian and free, hence flat, over the open-subgroup ring; apply the amalgam coherence theorem specified in the request.
Use coherence to close finitely presented modules under kernels and cokernels, then the finite-index calculus for G′.
acceptance: The conclusion is left coherence, not noetherianity of the noncompact augmented algebra.

nodes.title: Hom base change and residue fields of irreducibles
nodes.statement: If k is a finite field, L/k a field extension, V a finitely generated k[H]-module and W any k[H]-module, the natural map Hom_H(V,W)⊗_k L→Hom_H(V⊗L,W⊗L) is an isomorphism. For an admissible irreducible smooth k[H]-module pi, End_H(pi) is a finite extension k′/k, pi is absolutely irreducible as a k′-representation, and its scalar extension to an algebraic closure decomposes over the embeddings k′→kbar into pairwise nonisomorphic absolutely irreducible representations.

Admissibility puts the division endomorphism algebra inside the endomorphisms of finite-dimensional invariants; apply the finite-division-ring theorem.
Separate the embeddings of its finite centre after scalar extension and apply Schur descent.
acceptance: Finite generation of V is needed in the Hom statement; admissibility of pi is needed in the irreducible statement.

nodes.title: The compact-induction obstruction space
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite, G=GL_2(F), K=GL_2(O_F), and let W be a finite-dimensional smooth k[KZ]-module with central character. For a G-equivariant quotient q:c-Ind_{KZ}^G W→V set P^+={(a,b;0,1):a∈O_F\{0}, b∈O_F}, w=(0,1;varpi_F,0). Let I^+(W) be the span of standard generators [g,v] with g∈P^+,v∈W, and I^−(W)=wI^+(W). Put Delta(W,V)=q(I^+(W))∩q(I^−(W)) inside V. It is stable under IZ and w. It is an obstruction attached to this specified presentation, distinct from the finite Diamond invariant module D_1(rho).
proofSteps: Use the explicit two-cell coset decomposition to split the compact induction as I^+(W)⊕I^−(W).
Take the intersection of their images in V; the Iwahori decomposition preserves each image and w exchanges them, since w² is central.
Equivariant quotient maps preserve this intersection, so define its functorial map without asserting exactness for arbitrary sequences.
acceptance: Quotient functoriality does not imply right exactness: the augmentation from a compact induction to a trivial line has zero source obstruction and nonzero target obstruction.

nodes.statement: For G′=GL_2(Q_p)/⟨p I_2⟩, every irreducible smooth representation over a finite field k of characteristic p has a central character over k. The remaining F_p^× action splits over k, so a central eigenspace is all of the irreducible representation. This gives a k-valued character, rather than merely a character over an extension.

nodes.title: Finite length detected by the cosocle
nodes.statement: Let G′=GL_2(Q_p)/⟨p I_2⟩ and V be a finite-type smooth k[G′]-representation. Then V has finite length if and only if Hom_G′(V,pi′) is finite-dimensional for every irreducible pi′ and vanishes for all but finitely many isomorphism classes pi′. This is the finite-cosocle formulation of the admissible-cosocle criterion; it does not posit an algebraic maximal semisimple quotient for an arbitrary infinite-length object.
proofSteps: Reduce the finite filtration to quotients of I(sigma).

If a Serre-induction factor is infinite-length it retains I(sigma). Infinitely many pairwise distinct simple Hecke quotients of I(sigma), together with finite Ext support for the finite-length preceding factors, contradict finite support of Hom(V,pi′). Conversely finite length gives finite-dimensional Hom and finite support by the irreducible classification.
Finite length implies admissibility of the semisimple quotient by the Q_p irreducible classification.
acceptance: Neither finite type alone nor the same statement for arbitrary F is asserted.

nodes.title: Finite length detected by smooth vectors in the dual
nodes.statement: Let G′=GL_2(Q_p)/⟨p I_2⟩ and V a finite-type smooth k[G′]-representation. Give V^*=Hom_k(V,k) its compact pointwise topology and contragredient action; let (V^*)^sm be its smooth vectors. Then V has finite length iff dim_k (V^*)^sm is finite. Moreover, every finite-type infinite-length V admits a nonzero map V→I(sigma) for some Serre weight sigma.
proofSteps: Finite-length Q_p representations are admissible. Their compact dual M is finite over the noetherian k[[U]] for compact analytic U. Its smooth part is a k[[U]]-submodule, hence finitely generated; one open normal subgroup fixes its finitely many generators. It is therefore finite-dimensional over k, by the finite group algebra of the quotient. This is the elementary argument in Kohlhaase Remark 3.10.

For infinite length, use the Serre-induction filtration inductively to find a nonzero map from its infinite-length subobject into I(sigma). The resulting nonzero Hom-space is torsion-free over k[T] because I(sigma) is free over k[T], and is thus infinite-dimensional. Ext^1 from the preceding finite-length quotient into I(sigma) is finite-dimensional in the verified prime range. Its connecting map cannot be injective, giving V→I(sigma) nonzero. The recorded gap is exactly this Ext input at p=2,3.

Finite-support functionals in the compact dual of I(sigma) are smooth and dense, using the compact-induction coset decomposition and the finite weight action. If (V*)^sm is finite-dimensional it is closed, so the continuous dual map I(sigma)*→V* has finite-dimensional image. Dualising its nonzero image gives a finite-dimensional subrepresentation of I(sigma), impossible by the compact-induction rigidity argument.
acceptance: The smooth part of the compact dual, not the full algebraic dual dimension, is tested.

nodes.title: Emerton ordinary parts for GL_2(F)
nodes.statement: Let B=TN be the upper Borel of G=GL_2(F) and bar B its lower opposite. On admissible smooth primary torsion representations, use unnormalised smooth induction Ind_{bar B}^G and construct its right adjoint Ord_B. nodes.title: Finite obstruction and admissible length
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite characteristic-p field, with scalar extension to kbar permitted. For a finite-type smooth G=GL_2(F) representation V with central character and a finite-dimensional generating KZ-submodule W⊂V, the natural presentation c-Ind_{KZ}^G W→V has finitely generated kernel iff Delta(W,V) is finite-dimensional. This finite-kernel property holds for one such W iff it holds for every such W. If sigma is an irreducible KZ-weight and V is an admissible proper quotient of its compact induction with finite-dimensional Delta(sigma,V), then V has finite length.
proofSteps: Bound supports of a finite family of kernel generators in the radial coset decomposition; projection to the opposite half shows the obstruction lies in finitely many finite-dimensional radial spaces.

Conversely lift a basis of the finite obstruction in bounded radius. Subtract its translates to lower the support radius of any relation, proving the relations are finitely generated. Use the finite filtration of W to pass from an irreducible weight to general W.

For an admissible quotient choose an irreducible subrepresentation. The obstruction of that subrepresentation injects and is nonzero; the quotient obstruction is a quotient of the original. Thus its dimension strictly decreases. Admissibility passes to quotients in characteristic zero, so induction gives finite length.
Use finite coefficient extension and descent to transfer the algebraically closed coefficient argument to k.
acceptance: Properness and admissibility are essential in the final assertion: the entire compact induction has zero obstruction and infinite length.

nodes.title: Admissible finitely presented representations
nodes.statement: For any finite F/Q_p set G=GL_2(F). Let C_O(G) be the full subcategory of smooth primary torsion O[G]-representations that are both torsion-admissible and finitely presented in the compact-induction sense. Its objects have finite length and it is stable under subobjects, quotients and extensions. For F=Q_p it equals the finite-length category. For F≠Q_p its irreducible constituents, after finite scalar extension, are characters, twists of Steinberg and principal series, with no supersingular constituent.
proofSteps: Finite presentation bounds the coefficient exponent, so reduce through its finite residue-coefficient filtration. Admissibility implies local finiteness for the centre; enlarge coefficients so each finite generating KZ-module has a central-character composition series.

The obstruction-space criterion passes finite-dimensional obstruction to the irreducible-weight induction factors. Apply admissible finite-obstruction length to each factor, then the Hu–Vignéras filtration argument to obtain finite length.
Vignéras Proposition 5.5(i) gives admissibility and finite presentation for finite-length subobjects; combine quotient admissibility and the presentation calculus to obtain the Serre property.
For Q_p import finite presentation and admissibility of irreducibles. For F≠Q_p import Schraen–Wu to exclude supersingulars, then use the ordinary constituent classification and coefficient descent.
acceptance: Finite length and finite presentation are equivalent here only for F=Q_p.

nodes.title: Gelfand–Kirillov dimension of an admissible representation

nodes.title: Quotient and central-regular-sequence dimension comparison
nodes.statement: If a closed normal analytic subgroup N of a p-adic Lie group G acts trivially on an admissible smooth V, then dim_G V=dim_{G/N}V. In addition let H be analytic pro-p without p-torsion, A=k[[H]], and suppose gr_m A is Auslander-regular. If a homogeneous central regular sequence z_1,…,z_r generates J, gr_m A/J is a polynomial ring in dim H−r variables, and J annihilates gr M for a finite A-module M, then dim H−j_A(M) equals the support dimension of gr M over gr A/J.

Compare filtered and graded Ext grades by the requested filtered homological theorem.

acceptance: Do not use the commutative support formula for a noncommutative graded ring without killing the central regular sequence.

nodes.title: The crossing quotient algebra
nodes.statement: For a field k and finite index set J, define C_J(k)=k[X_i,Y_i:i∈J]/(X_iY_i:i∈J). Its Krull dimension is |J| and it is a commutative Cohen–Macaulay complete intersection. nodes.title: Adjoint tensor and finite projective weight structure

For a 3-deep lambda and sigma=F(lambda), A_i⊗P_sigma≅P_{F(lambda−alpha_i)}⊕P_sigma⊕P_{F(lambda+alpha_i)}. Tensoring sigma→soc P_sigma and cosoc P_sigma→sigma with A_i identifies the full socle and cosocle of this tensor. Also [P_sigma:sigma]=2^f, whereas [P_{F(lambda±alpha_i)}:sigma]=0. If Ptilde_sigma is its projective O[Gamma]-lift, then after a finite unramified coefficient extension splitting Gamma, Ptilde_sigma[1/p] is a sum of exactly 2^f pairwise nonisomorphic absolutely irreducible representations.

Identify the simple cosocle and hence the projective summands by Hom reciprocity and the corrected LMS22 Proposition 3.3(2). Every shifted weight here is a noncharacter; the corrected R_{mu} is therefore the claimed projective cover. Duality gives the socle statement.

The explicit principal-series and cuspidal Brauer-character calculation for Gamma makes the reduction of each characteristic-zero irreducible multiplicity-free.
